description: Attention: every query scores every key, the scores become probabilities, and each output is the values averaged with those probabilities; two matrix products and a softmax.

line_docs: All the scores at once: the inner product of Q with the transposed K, the matmul stone's +.×, divided by √d.
All the weights at once: the softmax stone's σ over every row of S.
All the outputs at once: the inner product of the weights with the values, +.× again.
m.purpose: +.× is the matmul stone's inner product, σ the softmax stone's placeholder glyph, ⍉ the transpose. Attention needs no primitive of its own; it is the composition the research calls R10, three lines over the stones already in the tour. Placeholder glyphs.
m.text:
S ← (Q +.× ⍉K) ÷ √d
P ← σ S
A ← P +.× V
m.title: The same three lines, composed from earlier stones

line_docs: The score of query i against key j: the dot product of row i of Q with row j of K, divided by √d.
The weights: softmax over row i of the scores, so query i's weights add up to one; entry j is how much it attends to key j.
The output for query i, feature k: every value row j, weighted by P_ij, added up.
math.purpose: Line one scores every query against every key, a dot product scaled by √d. Line two turns each row of scores into probabilities with softmax. Line three mixes the values with those probabilities: row i of A is the average of the rows of V, weighted by how much query i attends to each key. Two matrix products and a softmax, nothing new.
math.title: Scores, weights, output: three lines

name: attention

docs: How well query i matches key j: their dot product, scaled down by √d. One row per query; the row is what softmax sees.
Which token is asking. The stone's time axis walks the queries one at a time.
Which token is answering: runs over the keys in a score row, and is summed away in the output.
Which of the d features of a value: the columns of V and of A.
Definition: the left side is computed from the right side.
One row per token, d numbers each: what each token is looking for. Here 3 tokens of width 2.
Multiply paired entries: written by juxtaposition on the Math face, the × of the inner product +.× in the notation.
One row per token: what each token offers to be matched against. Kᵀ turns those rows into columns so every query meets every key.
Transpose: rows become columns. On paper a superscript T, in the notation ⍉.
Scale the scores down by √d so they do not grow with the width d and drive the softmax to one winner too soon. In the notation, ÷.
The square root of the width d.
How many features each query and key has; here 2. A dot product of d terms grows like √d, which is why the scores are divided by it.
Each row of scores turned into probabilities: how much query i attends to each key j. Every row adds up to one.
The softmax stone's function, applied to each row: exponentiate every score, divide by the row's sum. The same placeholder glyph σ as on that stone.
Row i is the values mixed by query i's weights: a weighted average of the rows of V, one output per token.
Add the weighted values over every key j: on paper a ∑ over j, in the notation the + of +.×.
One row per token: what each token passes on when it is attended to.

title: Attention

visual.purpose: The three input grids with the current query row lit, that query's score row and probability row as bars, and its output row filling in; the dataflow above is the composition: Q and K into +.×, ÷√d, σ, then +.× with V, into A.
visual.title: Q, K, V as grids; one query at a time
